- If sentiment history ends with a 1.00, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 1–2%.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon, especially after price spikes; apply downward bias to first 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >1.5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast peak at 1.2x prior high or adjust downward by 0.5–1.0%.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits mean-reversion bias — forecast tends to be too low in early days; add 0.3–0.8% to first 3–5 days.
- If true outcome shows strong upward momentum (e.g., >0.8% daily gain), model underreacts; increase forecast slope by 0.1–0.3% per day.
- Model often underestimates late-period volatility; add 0.2–0.5% to final 5–7 days if sentiment remains neutral or slightly positive.
- If model forecast is >10% above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward correction of 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
